case_id: L1 queue poison: Permanent fund loss via tiny withdrawal attacks

P.text: A normal user stakes the minimum allowed amount (10 gwei) and queues a withdrawal, creating a tiny L1 operation (1 in 8 decimals); the L1 bridge rejects the tiny amount.
P.evidence_quote: Staking the minimum allowed amount (10 gwei) => Queuing a withdrawal that creates a tiny L1 operation (1 in 8 decimals) => Permanently blocking all subsequent operations when the bridge rejects the tiny amount

I.text: The L1 operations queue should be able to skip failed operations, selectively reset the queue, retry operations, or override failures so a failed L1 operation does not irreversibly lock subsequent operations.
I.evidence_quote: When transactions in _processL1Withdrawals() or _processL1Deposits() fail, the contract cannot skip failed operations, reset the queue selectively, retry operations, or override failures.

V.text: When an L1 bridge call fails, the operation reverts and the processing index remains unchanged, so all subsequent operations become permanently stuck; resetting the queue deletes pending operations with no record, leaving users' ETH trapped and causing all users with pending withdrawals to permanently lose their funds.
V.evidence_quote: When a call to l1Write.sendTokenDelegate() fails, the operation reverts and the processing index remains unchanged. Since operations process sequentially, all subsequent operations become permanently stuck.
